rationale: The static parallel merge template (cvrp_parallel_merge_static/v1) exactly reproduces the Clarke-Wright (CW) baseline, which on dev_24 is the strongest raw method (16.22 mean) and remains best even after Relocate+2opt (16.14). Its iterative dynamic variant (cvrp_parallel_merge_dynamic/v1) has ~25 ms p95 and would consume >5% of budget but is structurally riskier at scale, whereas static stays ultra-fast (~7 ms p95, ~7.3 ms on n=200) with 100% completion and huge headroom under the 500 ms budget. The sequential construct template (cvrp_sequential_construct/v1) lags CW by ~10.7% remaining gap on dev_24, so it would waste evolution budget. Choosing static parallel merge gives the best quality head start with negligible timing pressure, leaving ample budget for evolution of merge heuristics or fast post-processing.
